title: Sustainability Intern – Social Impact (6 months)
description:
**JOB SUMMARY:**

The Sustainability Intern will have a strong interest in sustainability and social impact. They will support the execution of an industry leading factory responsibility program in home furnishings, working within the WSI sustainability team across Asia and the US.

The Social Compliance Intern will support the day-to-day operations of Williams-Sonoma, Inc.’s social compliance program with some addition projects. Working closely with the Sustainability team across Asia, the Intern will assist with social compliance audit tracking, supplier and factory follow-up, data management, reporting, documentation, and program coordination.

This role is suited for someone who is detail-oriented, comfortable working with data, and interested in gaining hands-on experience in the operational management of a global social compliance program.

**We are looking for an intern for 6months, starting January 2027, preferably able to commit to at least 4 days work week.**

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:**

* Support the day-to-day operation and coordination of WSI’s social compliance and factory responsibility program.
* Maintain and update social compliance records, trackers, databases, and supplier/factory information.
* Support follow-up with suppliers and factories on outstanding documentation, corrective actions, and program requirements.
* Support the preparation of social compliance reports.
* Support on Data Collection on Traceability for Europe and Pakistan market.
* Support on launching and tracking Vendor Progress for Annual Conflict Mineral Data Collection.

**DESIRABLE ATTRIBUTES, SKILLS AND QUALIFICATIONS:**

* Strong interest in social compliance, responsible sourcing, sustainability, or global supply chains.
* Embodies the highest level of personal and professional integrity and ethics.
* A true passion for sustainability.
* Maintains a global perspective and is culturally sensitive and aware.
* Thrives in a collaborative team environment.
* Demonstrates a creative, energetic and motivated spirit.
* Possesses attention to detail while managing simultaneous projects in a dynamic environment.
* Strong data analysis and excel skills
* Ability to work independently and cooperatively in a diverse group
* Fluency in English and proficiency in Microsoft Word, PowerPoint, Excel
* Proficiency in Microsoft BI is a plus.

**Commitment period:**

* Minimum able to commit to 4 full days a week, ideally for 6 months.
* This internship can be a credit-bearing internship with the academic institutions.

#LI-KW1

  

**About Us**

Founded in 1956, Williams-Sonoma, Inc. is the premier specialty retailer of home furnishings in the United States, Canada, Puerto Rico, Australia, United Kingdom and the rest of the world with franchise partnerships. Our family of brands are Williams-Sonoma, Pottery Barn, Pottery Barn Kids, PBteen, West Elm, Williams-Sonoma Home, Rejuvenation, Mark and Graham, and GreenRow. Our passion for high-quality products, functional design, outstanding customer service, enhancing the lives of our customers and the communities remains as our core values.

Today, we are a more than USD 8.7 billion company, with a multi-brand, multi-channel, global enterprise supported by state-of-the-art technology and some of the most talented teams in retailing - and we're always looking for new energy and ideas.

The Singapore regional office was set up in 2008 and we currently have more than 160 associates in functions such as sustainability, customs & compliance, finance, human resource, information technology, inventory planning, logistics, sourcing and quality assurance.

title: Research Associate (AI for Nature Based Climate Solutions)
description:
ASE is a diverse school focusing on the connections between geosciences, ecology, society and Earth systems. Our approach integrates these disciplines to examine big environmental challenges both in Southeast Asia and globally. We conduct cutting-edge research on topics that include ecology, geohazards, climate change, sea-level rise, environmental sustainability, conservation of environment and biodiversity, and interactions between environment and society. For more information on ASE please visit https://www.ntu.edu.sg/ase .

The Yanyan Cheng research group is seeking a Research Associate. This position is part of a Singapore MOE funded research project hosted by ASE. The Research Associate will help advance research in integrated assessment modeling and understand interactions among land, water, carbon, energy, climate, ecosystems, and human systems.

This is a one-year appointment and potentially renewable based on performance and funding availability.

**Key Responsibilities:**

* Collect, curate, validate, and document large-scale multimodal ecohydrological remote sensing datasets.
* Train and evaluate models on large datasets and high-performance computing systems; establish reproducible baselines, ablation studies, and evaluation suites.
Apply the developed datasets and models to the monitoring and analysis of tropical ecohydrological processes.  

**Job Requirements:**

* The candidate should hold a master's degree in information and communication engineering, with research experience in 3D point-cloud or point-cloud sequence processing, is highly desirable.
* The candidate should posse extensive relevant experience in model design and development, programming implementation, experimental design and evaluation, and peer-reviewed scientific writing.
* The candidate should have demonstrated research expertise in both remote sensing and computer vision.
* The candidate should have a strong publication record. Preference will be given to candidates with first- or co-first-author papers in CCF Rank A computer science venues (e.g., CVPR) and leading peer-reviewed remote sensing journals (e.g., IEEE TGRS).
* The candidate should have strong programming skills in Python and MATLAB, together with practical experience in deep-learning frameworks such as PyTorch, remote sensing data processing, Linux environments, and high-performance computing.
* The candidate must be able to communicate fluently and demonstrate strong academic writing skills for papers, reports, and presentations.
* The candidate should be able to work independently and collaboratively, manage large datasets and research codebases, meet project deadlines, and produce reproducible research outputs.
Interpersonal skill (e.g. Ability to work independently / develop solutions under strict timelines, meticulous and eye for details / excellent organizational / time management skills).  

ASE seeks a diverse and inclusive workforce and is committed to equality of opportunity. We welcome applications from all and recruit on the basis of merit, regardless of age, race, gender, religion, marital status and family responsibilities, or disability.

We regret to inform that only shortlisted candidates will be notified.

At Alstom, we understand transport networks and what moves people. From high-speed trains, metros, monorails, and trams, to turnkey systems, services, infrastructure, signalling and digital mobility, we offer our diverse customers the broadest portfolio in the industry. Every day, 80,000 colleagues lead the way to greener and smarter mobility worldwide, connecting cities as we reduce carbon and replace cars.

Could you be the full-time **Cluster Communications & CSR Director iEast Asia** we’re looking for?

**Your future role**

Take on a new challenge and apply your strategic communications and corporate social responsibility expertise in a new cutting-edge field. You’ll work alongside dynamic, collaborative, and forward-thinking teammates.

You'll play a pivotal role in shaping Alstom’s image and fostering business growth across the country and emerging territories in East Asia. Day-to-day, you’ll work closely with teams across the business (HR, project teams, Corporate/Sector publications), build trust with key stakeholders, and drive impactful initiatives that align with Alstom’s values and goals.

You’ll specifically take care of internal and external communications strategies, but also develop CSR programs that engage employees and enhance Alstom’s social impact.

* Driving media relations, including press releases, press conferences, and social media presence.
* Supporting crisis communications at the country level.
* Organizing and managing internal and external events to enhance Alstom’s visibility and engagement.
* Managing branding and visual identity to align with Alstom’s corporate standards.
* Building CSR and employee volunteering programs and fostering relationships with NGOs.
* Leading a team and managing PR agencies and budgets effectively.
  

**All about you**

We value passion and attitude over experience. That’s why we don’t expect you to have every single skill. Instead, we’ve listed some that we think will help you succeed and grow in this role:

* Educational background in PR, Marketing, or Communications.
* 15-18 years of experience in communications.
* Experience working with manufacturing or heavy engineering industries with a strong B2G (Business-to-Government) connection is highly desirable.
* Prior experience in journalism or at a PR/Corporate Affairs agency.
* Experience working in matrix organizations is a plus.
* Strong understanding of internal and external communication strategies.
* Proficiency in managing cross-functional teams and budgets.

* Enjoy stability, challenges, and a long-term career free from boring daily routines.
* Work with cutting-edge communication and CSR strategies that drive meaningful impact.
* Collaborate with transverse teams and helpful colleagues.
* Contribute to innovative projects that shape the future of mobility.
* Utilise our inclusive and collaborative working environment.
* Steer your career in whatever direction you choose across functions and countries.
* Benefit from our investment in your development, through award-winning learning.
* Progress towards senior leadership positions within Alstom.
* Benefit from a fair and dynamic reward package that recognises your performance and potential, plus comprehensive and competitive social coverage (life, medical, pension).

You don’t need to be a train enthusiast to thrive with us. We guarantee that when you step onto one of our trains with your friends or family, you’ll be proud. If you’re up for the challenge, we’d love to hear from you!

**Important to note**

As a global business, we’re an equal-opportunity employer that celebrates diversity across the 63 countries we operate in. We’re committed to creating an inclusive workplace for everyone.

description:
As an Export Credit Agency, Export Development Canada (EDC) helps Canadian companies of all sizes succeed on the world stage. With this goal in mind, EDC aims to increase trade opportunities in the Asia-Pacific region through growing our local presence in Singapore with a variety of locally-offered services.
  
  
The EDC branch office in Singapore serves as a hub for the Asia-Pacific region. The branch allows us to support our Asia-Pacific and Canadian customers more effectively as they go, grow and succeed internationally.
  
  
At EDC, we view Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) as a competitive advantage for ourselves and our customers. Through our deep subject matter expertise, we support organizations of all sizes to evolve their responsible business practices as a means of improving their competitive position. Most of our Environmental and Social Risk Management (ESRM) team resides in Canada, but we have a Singapore team that is expanding to accelerate the impact we can have in the Asia-Pacific region through local expertise and timely support.
  
  
Job Overview
  
  
The EDC Singapore branch office is seeking a motivated and resourceful person to join our ESRM team as an Senior Environmental and Social (E&S) Risk Advisor for the Asia-Pacific region. The ESRM team is responsible for helping fulfill EDC's commitments to conduct business in a responsible and ethical manner and integrate our ESG values into the business we do. The Senior E&S Risk Advisor will be responsible for conducting due diligence on the business we support for our customers doing business or looking to expand into the Asia-Pacific region. Our vision for this role is to be an integral part of the business team to help manage relationships with our customers and partners and guide them on their ESG journey and ensure this journey is reflective of the E&S risks in their business. The role will be supported through close collaboration with the head office in Ottawa.
  
  
This is an opportunity for an individual who is a resourceful E&S risk analyst, who can form strong relationships with EDC clients in the Asia-Pacific region, EDC business teams and ESRM colleagues, whether based in Singapore, the Asia-Pacific region or Canada and who thrives in a dynamic environment.
  
  
Key Responsibilities
  
  
Leads the assessment of EDC transactions, identifying material E&S risks and recommending key mitigants for EDC's financing transactions. Applies the Equator Principles, the IFC Performance Standards, the UNGPs and other international standards as relevant.
  
  
Analyzes and determines the adequacy of ESIAs, ESDD reports, monitoring reports, thematic reports (e.g., biodiversity, archeology, human rights), environmental and social action plans (ESAPs), audit reports, consultant terms of reference, request for proposals, E&S-related policies with the aim of managing E&S risks and promoting alignment with good practice and international standards
  
  
In collaboration with EDC business teams, negotiates with EDC clients the incorporation of E&S commitments in financing documentation to prevent, mitigate, or address the E&S risks on EDC's commercial transactions
  
  
Manages relationships with diverse stakeholders, including internal and external clients, co-lending IFIs, DFIs, and ECAs and consultants, building high levels of professional credibility and mutual trust
  
  
Undertakes site visits, assessing E&S capacity and performance in the field within the Asia-Pacific Region (typical 1-6 days, 1-5 times per year)
  
  
Monitors transaction / project performance over time, identifying and resolving issues of non-compliance with E&S commitments.
  
  
As a subject matter expert, advises management and senior management on a range of E&S issues, including those prevalent in the Asia-Pacific Region, making authoritative technical and professional recommendations to improve the improve the E&S performance of EDC's transactions.
  
  
Produces and/or edit documents in line with organizational-style guidelines and prepares information for consumption by EDC risk management committees, business teams, senior management and/or external clients
  
  
Provide specialist advice on the interpretation and application of ESRM policies, procedures, programs and/or products to EDC underwriting teams, business teams and others, to resolve complex or contentious queries and issues and enable others to take appropriate actions
  
  
Maintain and renew a deep knowledge and understanding of the organization's ESRM policies and procedures and of relevant regulatory codes and codes of conduct, and ensure transactions adhere to required standards.
  
  
Develop an understanding of EDC's mandate, Asia-Pacific strategic focus and financing products, and identify opportunities to advance the sustainability agenda with clients in the region.
  
  
Occasionally support EDC on non-transactional E&S-related interactions with relevant external stakeholders
  
  
What We Are Looking For
  
  
Completion of a degree in environmental or social sciences or in a sub-discipline such as ecology, environmental management, environmental and social risk management, climate change, biodiversity, water resources, international development, sustainable development, human rights, gender studies, occupational health and safety, community relations & resettlement, law (environmental or human rights) or engineering.
  
  
Advanced knowledge in ESIA and/or due diligence principles, frameworks and standards, including the Equator Principles and the IFC Performance Standards
  
  
Excellent communication and demonstrated ability to manage relationships with customers and stakeholders
  
  
Minimum of 7-10 years' experience in ESIA or ESDD in the consulting space or equivalent industry experience within EDC-relevant business sectors (e.g. Extractive Industries, Agrifoods, Advance Manufacturing, Clean Tech and Renewable Energy, Apparel, utilities and Infrastructure)
  
  
Evidence of success in prioritizing and meeting deadlines in an environment that requires managing multiple competing tasks and responsibilities.
  
  
Evidence of ability to discern, distill, and concisely and clearly communicate (written and verbally) key issues in complex business transactions and provide advice based on client needs
  
  
Fluent in English for oral communication as well as reading and writing
  
  
Ability and willingness to travel up to 20% of working hours
  
  
Ability to work independently and collaboratively across geographies and time zones.
  
  
What Will Make You Stand Out
  
  
Expertise in social impact assessment or biodiversity impact assessment.
  
  
Experience working as an independent E&S consultant on behalf of lenders or in the financial services industry, on behalf of private sector companies in major project development or working at or with international finance institutions (Financial Institutions abiding to Equator Principles, Export Credit Agencies, Development Finance Institutions, Multilateral Development Banks)
  
  
In addition to English, can communicate in one or more local Asia-Pacific language
  
  
Degree, diploma or training in Business, Finance, or related disciplines
  
  
Export Development Canada (EDC) is a Crown corporation dedicated to helping Canadian companies of all sizes succeed on the world stage. We equip them with the tools they need – the trade knowledge, financial solutions, equity, insurance, and connections – to grow their business with confidence. This in turn, creates jobs and increases prosperity at home.
  
  
As international risk experts, we help Canadian companies to navigate, manage and take on risk to support their growth beyond Canada’s borders. Since 1944, businesses of all sizes and sectors have counted on us for the export knowledge and financial solutions they need to succeed in global markets. Beyond our solutions, we believe that sustainable, responsible and inclusive trade is a powerful force for good in Canada and around the world, and that’s what drives us.
  
  
**Our solutions include:**  
Capital – access to working capital and financing
  
  
Risk mitigation – insurance that lowers the risk of doing business abroad
  
  
Trade knowledge – expertise to help companies make informed decisions
  
  
Global connections – relationships that connect Canadian and international companies and help both parties grow
  
  
International Footprint
  
  
With offices across Canada and around the world, we are close to the Canadian businesses we support and to the buyers in global markets that can connect Canadian exporters to international supply chains.
